M: The city wall. Somebody has carved STRENGTH into every fifth stone.
I: Stone, thick and square. Nothing in this city was built to look pretty. Everything was built to last.
H: A cottage. The garden is mostly practice dummies.
1: The Kaloseum's great gate. Carved over the arch: HERE WE TEST OURSELVES.
2: The chapel. A lantern burns in the window.
3: The library. A sign: QUIET. (Somebody has added: PLEASE.)
4: The Adventurers' Guild. A notice board, crowded with jobs.
5: The hospital. It smells of herbs and soap.
7: The store. EVERYTHING YOU NEED, MOSTLY.
8: The horse barn. Something inside is chewing very loudly.
>: East: a bridge, and beyond it the Mage kingdom.
^: North: the road to the castle.
_: South: down toward the old mines, and an overgrown garden.
C: The Kaloseum. Thousands of seats, and every one of them has seen a fight.
K: The statue of Kaldor, colossal, one boot on a broken crown.
The plaque: KALDOR THE KINGBREAKER. Undying.
P: The chapel. A bell hangs in the tower, and the window glows in every colour.
B: The library. Columns, and a great book over the door.
N: The Adventurers' Guild. The notice board is crowded with jobs.
V: The hospital. Clean white walls, and a sign with a green leaf.
W: The tavern. Singing, slightly off-key, and the smell of stew.
a: The store. EVERYTHING YOU NEED, MOSTLY.
r: The horse barn. Something inside is chewing very loudly.
z: The training ground's sand, raked flat and stamped flat again.
e: A straw dummy. It has been hit so often it has started to look smug.
k: A rack of practice weapons, all wood, all chipped.
g: The paddock. The grass is shorter than it should be.
u: A cottage. Window boxes, and a practice dummy in nearly every garden.
9: The Bank of Warrior City. Over the door, in gold: STRENGTH IS WEALTH. Under it, smaller: WEALTH IS ALSO WEALTH.
$: The Bank of Warrior City. Pale stone, gold trim, not a scratch on it. The only building in town nobody has punched.
X: The bakery wall. Still standing. Give it time.
Plaster, white with flour from the floor up to where the ceiling used to start. A corner of the roof is still up there, hanging on by its nails. A pigeon looks down from it. It doesn't come down.
R: Roof. Tiles, laths, a rafter and half a chimney pot. It all came in with him, and stayed when he left.
A loaf is sticking out of the bottom of the pile. It's fine. It's flat, but it's fine.
w: A crater in the floor, the shape of a very large man. Arms out. Legs out. A deeper dent where the head went.
The flagstones are cracked in a ring round it. Somebody has swept right up to the edge, very carefully, and not one inch further.
Q: The bread oven, brick, and still lit. Still warm. Still baking, as far as anyone can tell, out of habit.
It's the one thing in here he missed.
f: A sack of flour, burst. Most of it is on the floor. Some of it is on the walls.
A surprising amount of it went up, onto the ceiling. The ceiling isn't there. Nobody knows where that lot went.
l: The counter, snapped in the middle. Loaves along it, every one of them flat now. Each has a new label in the same tired hand: FLATBREAD.
n: Mistress Hettie's tray, on an upturned crate. Buns, pressed thin as coins, still for sale. A card: SECONDS. Under it, in pencil: THIRDS.

objects.name: Barnaby Loudmouth
lines: HEAR YE! Welcome to Warrior City, home of the KALOSEUM!
Fights every night. Glory every fight. Seats... mostly every seat.

answer: The last man to call out the king was Aurek. Aurek the Tall. Tallest thing in the city, after the Kaloseum. The king put him down in front of everyone.
Here, the strongest rules. Aurek lost, so Aurek serves. Never complains. Never smiles. Does the job. You'll see.

questions.ask: Loudmouth? Bit on the nose, isn't it?
answer: IT'S A FAMILY NAME AND WE ARE VERY PROUD OF IT!
My nan cracked the chapel window once. Twice, counting the echo.

lines: THE CHAMPION! In MY city! The one who sent the Warden over the banners!
Your name's on the wall. In chalk, but on the wall.

objects.name: The Traveler
lines: Oh! Hello, hello! Lovely day for it.
A signpost, all arms.
EAST: THE KALOSEUM. NORTH: THE DESERTERS' CAMP AND THE OLD FORT. SOUTH: THE ROYAL GARDEN, THE OLD MINE.
WEST: THE COURIER ROAD. Somebody has added, in chalk: MIND THE BOULDERS.
A signpost outside the Kaloseum.
NORTH: THE ROAD NORTH, THE DESERTERS' CAMP, THE OLD FORT. (The gate's shut till you're overall Lv 10.)
SOUTH: THE ROYAL GARDEN, THE OLD MINE. WEST: THE COURIER ROAD.
EAST: THE BRIDGE TO THE MAGE KINGDOM. Under it, a smaller sign: UNDER CONSTRUCTION. SORRY.

objects.name: Watchman Kell
lines: Round the Kaloseum, on and on. Dorr does the other side.
We've never met. We're always exactly opposite. I've heard he's tall.

answer: Trouble. In Warrior City, trouble is everyone. So I watch everyone.
Mostly they're fighting. I only step in if somebody's losing badly. Then I take notes for the Yard.
Once, nearly. He stopped to tie his boot. I nearly caught him up.
Then I stopped to tie mine. Professional courtesy. Ruined it.

questions.ask: Dorr sounds more interesting than you.
answer: …He probably is. He's tall.
* Kell marches on round the Kaloseum. A bit sadly.

objects.name: Watchman Dorr
lines: Keep moving. Keep it civil. Keep your purse somewhere I can't see it.
That's for your safety, not mine. Mine's fine.

answer: Everybody's out to get everybody. Only the strong get to keep their boots.
I'd tie yours on, if I were you. Tightly. Twice.
Kell's a myth. A story they tell new watchmen.
Somebody leaves bootprints round the Kaloseum, always just ahead of me. I've never seen him. I've never wanted to.

questions.ask: You're not very tall, are you?
answer: Who told you I was tall?
…Kell. It was Kell, wasn't it.

objects.name: Haldor the Hand
lines: Oi. You looking at me? Look harder. Now FIGHT me.
Not here. Not now. Later. I'll find you. I find everyone.

answer: You only need one to win a fight. I keep the other for my dinner.
Lost to a man with two hands, once. He's up north now, at the camp. I'm here. Hands aren't everything.
The culling games. Eighteen next spring. I go into the Kaloseum, I come out a champion.
Champions get a house by the king, a statue, and every woman in the city smiling at them. I've practised my smile.
* He smiles. It's frightening.
LITTLE?
* He goes red, then redder, then a colour you've only seen on beetroot. He stomps off to punch a wall. The wall wins.

objects.name: Sigrun
lines: Kaloseum, third round. Spear through the shoulder. Here. Look. LOOK.
BEKK: Pfft. Bit of a hole. Check THIS.

answer: Me. Twenty-nine.
BEKK: Thirty.
One of yours is a tattoo of a scar, Bekk.
BEKK: Still counts.
Scars mean you lived. Living means you were strong. Strong means you live by the king.
Simple maths. The only maths we do here.

questions.ask: Did you lose all those fights?
answer: I LIVED through all those fights. That's winning.
…Most of them were winning. A few were a draw with a wall.

objects.name: Bekk
lines: Every scar's a story. Every story's me winning. I've changed some of them a bit.

answer: This one. The culling games, the year I turned eighteen. I fought my best friend.
He's got the matching one. Up north, at the camp. We write. Well. I write.

questions.ask: Is the tattoo really a scar?
answer: It's a scar of a tattoo of a scar. Very rare. Hurt twice.
They ARE made up. That's what a story is.
* He counts his scars on his fingers, runs out of fingers, and looks at you as if that's your fault.

objects.name: Measuring Molly
lines: Biceps measured! A copper a bicep, two for the pair, three if you want me to lie.
Most people pay three.

questions.ask: Who has the biggest arms in the city?
answer: Champion Vorn, up in Kaldorhold. Twenty-two inches. I had to borrow a second tape.
He paid me in a lock of his hair. I've had offers for it. Serious offers. From serious women.
* She wraps the tape round your arm, squints, and writes something down.
Hm. Lovely. You'll want to pay the three.
Course it has. Everybody's tape's stretched. That's how you sell a tape.
…Don't tell Torvald.

objects.name: Torvald
lines: * He's flexing so hard his ears have gone white.
Go on, Molly. Say it. Say the number.

answer: Nineteen. Nineteen and a half if she's feeling kind. Twenty if I pay.
Twenty gets you looked at in the plaza. Twenty-two gets you a wife. Twenty-five gets you a statue.

questions.ask: Why do you want bigger arms?
answer: So the right people notice. The ladies by the Kaloseum rank us all, every morning. There's a list.
I'm on it. Near the bottom. Under a horse. The horse has a lovely build.

questions.ask: All that muscle and nothing upstairs.
answer: Upstairs? I'm not allowed upstairs. I'm not ranked high enough.
* He keeps flexing. His ears go whiter.

objects.name: Lady Odessa
lines: Shh. We're ranking.
Champion Vorn, first. Champion Vorn's cousin, second. A very large horse, eleventh. Torvald, twelfth.

answer: Men. By Kaloseum standing first, then arms, then whether they still have their own teeth.
Every woman in the city wants the strongest man. The mother of a champion lives like a goddess. Nobody ever tells her no.
* She looks you up and down. Then down. Then down a bit further.
You're not on the list, darling. You're not on the page. You're on the floor, where the list fell.
Shallow? Darling, I'm practical. Looks fade. Champions get statues.
* She turns back to the plaza, and ranks you, out loud, below the bench.

objects.name: Brisa
lines: Ooh. Ooh! Did you see his arms? No, not him. Behind him. No, he's gone.
I only like a man if the Kaloseum likes him first.

questions.ask: What's the Kaloseum got to do with love?
answer: Everything! At eighteen they go in. Only the strongest come out champions.
A champion lives by the king and fathers as many children as he likes, all of them strong. That's not love. That's an investment.
Champion Vorn smiled at me once! Well. Near me. At a pie behind me.
I've kept the pie. I shan't be eating it. It's been six weeks.

questions.ask: Champions wouldn't look twice at you.
answer: They looked once, though! Near enough!
* She fans herself, wounded, and writes your name at the very bottom of a very long list.

objects.name: Fenna Fairbrow
lines: I do my hair every morning, in case a champion walks by. It takes four hours.
A champion walks by about once a year. It's a lot of hair for once a year.

answer: Mothers of champions are treated like goddesses. Statues. Songs. A chair carried by four men, everywhere.
I'd like a chair carried by four men. My feet hurt. Strength is everything, but so are feet.

questions.ask: What about the rest of us?
answer: You?
* She looks at you, then at your friends, then back at the plaza.
I'm sure you're all very nice. Nice doesn't get you a chair.
FOUR HOURS. And the wind does what it likes with it.
The wind's not on the list either.

objects.name: Lord Gilder
lines: Out of the way, please. That's my shadow you're standing in. I paid for it.
My son is a champion. Three years running. We live by the king now. Everything is gold. Even the things that shouldn't be.

answer: The doorknobs. The cutlery. The bath. The dog's bowl. The dog's coat.
The dog can't get up in it. He seems to like that.

questions.ask: Why are you down here, then?
answer: Visiting the poor. Once a year, to remind them what to aim for.
Also my son fights tonight, and the good seats are down here. The poor get the best view. It's the one thing they've got.

questions.ask: What happened to your son's rivals?
answer: Lost. The culling games: the strong go on, the rest don't. That's the whole idea, dear.
Their families live up north now, I think. I don't go north. There's no gold.

questions.ask: You didn't earn a penny of that.
answer: Of course not. My son did. With his fists. On other people's sons.
That's earning, in Warrior City. You're thinking of somewhere soft.

objects.name: Old Hessa
lines: Going south? Past the Royal Garden? Don't.
Don't go into the forest. Stay on the road. If the road goes into the forest, stay on a different road.

answer: Lights in the trees, at night, low down. Where nobody would carry a lantern.
Figures, standing just off the path. Still. You look again, they're trees. You look a third time, you're running.
And a boy crying, deep in. A woodcutter heard him and went to help. Found nobody. Heard him all the way home.
The old graves, by the chapel in the Berserker Kingdom. The sexton found some open.
Not dug up. Dug OUT. The earth thrown up and out, like something left in a hurry.
Badgers, he said. He's moved to a town with no badgers.
I believe in roads. Roads have never once dug themselves up.
Could be nothing. Foxes and fog and a lad with a sad dog. I don't need to know which.
Old, yes. Bat, no. Superstitious, absolutely. And I'm still alive, aren't I?
* She turns her back on you, and on the south road, firmly.

objects.name: Sergeant Morda
lines: Again. Again. AGAIN. Lisbet, he's not made of glass. Hit him properly.
The Yard at Kaldorhold takes them at twelve. I get them the week before, so they turn up knowing which end to hold.

questions.ask: What happens to the ones who aren't strong enough?
answer: North. The deserters' camp. Little food, no money, no way back.
I don't decide. The Yard decides. I just stand here and shout until it's obvious.
Like? I don't do like. I do Tuesdays, and then I do Wednesdays.
…The odd one makes it. Becomes a champion. Sends me a fruit basket. I eat it alone, in the dark. Lovely.
Shouting's the kind part. The Kaloseum doesn't shout.
AGAIN, LISBET.

objects.name: Lisbet
lines: HYAH! Sorry, Dunstan. HYAH! Sorry.
I'm twelve next week. Then it's the Yard. I'm getting my sorries out now.

questions.ask: Are you scared of the Yard?
answer: No. Yes. My big sister went. She's a champion now. Mum gets bowed at in the street.
My other sister went too. Mum doesn't talk about her. She's up north.

questions.ask: Why do you keep saying sorry?
answer: Sergeant says sorry's for the weak. So I'm using them all up before I go. I've about forty left.

questions.ask: You'll end up up north too.
answer: I WON'T.
* She hits Dunstan, hard, and doesn't say sorry. Then says it, very quietly.

objects.name: Dunstan
lines: I'm being a good target. Sergeant says I'm the best target she's ever had.
I think that's a compliment. I've decided it's a compliment.

questions.ask: Do you want to go to the Yard?
answer: Course! Strong kids get their families a house by the king. My nan's never had a house with a floor.
She's got very excited about the floor.

questions.ask: You'll get stronger. Keep at it.
answer: I will! I'll get so strong I can carry Nan AND the floor.

questions.ask: Best target, eh? Says it all.
answer: …It's a compliment.
* His wooden sword droops. Lisbet pats his helmet. Then hits it.

objects.name: Master Albin
lines: Morning. We're open.
* Behind him, his bakery has no roof. A bit more of it comes down while you watch.
Flatbread? Very flat. Today's special. Yesterday it was a cottage loaf.

answer: Second batch had just gone in. Then a very large man came through the roof.
Out of the sky. From the direction of the Kaloseum. In chains. It's not how people usually come in.
He landed on the bread. Then on the floor. Then a bit further into the floor.
Carried away by soldiers, shortly after he landed.
It took six of them. They didn't pay for the roof. Or the buns.
One of them took a bun on the way out. You don't argue with six men carrying a seventh.
Nobody. We were all out the back, arguing about the rye.
The bread got hurt. The bread got very hurt.
And him, I suppose. He was past saying.
The Warden, Hettie says. Out of the Kaloseum. Big as a door, and chained like one.
Word is somebody in the arena hit him. Once. I'd like to meet whoever it was.
I'd like to give him the bill.

questions.ask: Maybe bake something lighter next time.
answer: * He looks at you for a long time.
I'll write that down.
* He doesn't write it down.

objects.name: Mistress Hettie
lines: Buns. They were two coppers. They spent the morning under a very large man, so now they're one.
They're very thin buns. You get more of them to a bag.

answer: We're fine. The shop isn't. The shop's having a lie-down.
Albin keeps going back in to check on the oven. The oven's fine. It's the only thing in there that is.
With what? The roof money was in the till. The till was under him.
We wrote to the Kaloseum. They wrote back. It said STRENGTH ABOVE EVERYTHING.
That isn't a sum. I checked.
It is. Lovely light.
* She goes back to dusting the flour off a bun. Under the flour is more flour.

objects.name: Little Tansy
lines: A man fell out of the sky onto our house. He went in the floor. Nobody else in my class has seen that.
I'm selling crumbs. A copper a bag. They're the bread from before.

answer: A big man, ever so high up, going AAAAAAA.
Then he stopped going AAAAAAA, and the roof went, and Dad said a word I'm not allowed.

questions.ask: I'll take a bag of crumbs.
answer: That's a copper. You can owe me.
Everybody owes us. The soldiers owe us a roof.

questions.ask: I bet your bread's what knocked him out.
answer: It is NOT. Our bread's soft. Dad says.
* She looks up at where the roof was. She looks less sure.

lines: The bakery's sign, hanging by one chain. A painted loaf, and under it: ALBIN & DAUGHTER. FRESH DAILY.
Somebody has chalked a line through FRESH DAILY and written: OPEN. ROOF CLOSED.

objects.name: Bryony
lines: * The apprentice is sweeping flour off the path. The wind brings a little more out of the bakery. She sweeps that too.
Mind the hole. The one in the floor. The one in the roof isn't a hole any more. It's just the sky.

answer: Master Albin said keep the place tidy. I'm the apprentice. I don't get to decide when a place is past tidy.
It's past tidy.
Nobody's had the heart to put it out. It's done four batches since. There's nowhere to put them.
So I've been eating them. I'm the nowhere.
* She looks at the crater the shape of a man.
Yes. Yes, I did.
